title: House of the Rising Sun
summary: Am, C, D, F and E in a rolling 6/8. The classic picked-arpeggio workout, plus a gentle push into the full F barre and some minor-chord colours.
skills: The F chord, easy and full barre
notes: Traditional song. Parts are practice arrangements.

sections.name: Verse
sections.chords: Am | C | D | F | Am | C | E | E | Am | C | D | F | Am | E | Am | E

lessons.title: Rolling arpeggios
lessons.goal: Pick bass, 3, 2, 1, 2, 3 in every bar while the chord rings.
body: Hold the whole chord shape and pick one string at a time. B in the pattern means the chord's lowest string: the A string for Am and C, the D string for D and F, the low E for E.
Count it in two big beats, ONE-and-a TWO-and-a. That rolling feel is 6/8.
steps: Play along at 100 with the picked arpeggio.
Mute rhythm guitar and keep it rolling on your own.
Let the notes ring into each other. Don't lift fingers until the chord changes.

lessons.title: From easy F to the full barre
lessons.goal: Swap the four-string F for the full barre without losing time.
body: The easy F (xx3211) is a small barre on the top two strings. The full barre (133211) is an E-shape at the 1st fret, the hardest place on the neck to barre because the frets are widest.
Same E shape you used for the A chord in Fire on the Mountain, just slid down to the 1st fret.
steps: Play the picked arpeggio with the easy F.
Switch to the "Full F barre" variation and play along.
If it buzzes, roll your index finger slightly onto its bony edge.

lessons.title: Minor and seventh colours
lessons.goal: Hear what one added note does to each chord.
body: Am7 is Am with one finger lifted. Cmaj7 and Fmaj7 add the major seventh, D7 and E7 add the flat seventh. The progression is the same, but the mood softens.
Turn the fretboard labels to intervals to see the 7 or b7 appear in each shape.
steps: Alternate the plain arpeggio and "Seventh colours" every pass.
Pick your favourite colour for each chord and mix them.

lessons.title: Why E major?
lessons.goal: See the G# that the E chord brings into A minor.
body: In plain A minor the five chord would be Em, with a G. This song uses E major, with a G#, which pulls hard back to A. That raised seventh is called harmonic minor.
When you play melodies over the E chord, use G# instead of G.
steps: Set the fretboard to Chord tones and watch the third over E.
Switch the scale to harmonic minor and compare it to natural minor.

lessons.title: A minor pentatonic over the changes
lessons.goal: Play fills from box 1 at the 5th fret.
body: A minor pentatonic at the 5th fret is the box most guitarists know first. It works over every chord here except one note: over E, avoid the C and lean on B and E instead.
steps: Loop the pentatonic fill and learn it from the tab.
Mute it and answer each line of the progression with your own short fill.

lessons.title: Two hands in 6/8
lessons.goal: Left hand on 1 and 4, right hand on the four eighths in between.
body: Count ONE-two-three FOUR-five-six. The left hand plays the root on ONE and the fifth on FOUR; the right hand plays the chord on two, three, five and six.
Watch the E chord: the right hand needs G#, not G.
steps: Mute keys and play both with the band at 100.

lessons.title: Broken chords in the right hand
lessons.goal: Play each chord one note at a time: root, third, fifth, octave, fifth, third.
body: This is the keyboard version of the guitar arpeggio. Keep your hand in one position per chord and let the notes ring with the sustain pedal if you have one.
steps: Try it with your left hand adding the root on beat one.
